assets.scene_prompt: Primary request: a baseball stadium GAME CENTER concourse / viewing and match-analysis room, visually distinct from an office and from a generic video lounge. The northern wall opens through large windows overlooking a baseball diamond and stands, still seen in the same pixel-RPG projection. A north-wall physical SCHEDULE scoreboard with schematic matchup tiles (no real teams, dates or scores) is the main focal object. The upper-left side has an accessible ANALYSIS workbench with a small array of monitors showing a baseball diamond, lineup rows, a strike zone and simple pitch-shape icons, all part of one console; player can stand on the clear floor south of it. The upper-right side has an IN GAME screen for historical ball-path and corresponding pitch video, with an adjacent small control desk; show a stylized strike zone / baseball field with a curved ball line, not people and not a synthetic mini-game. A few short empty spectator benches and small baseball memorabilia shelves hug the OUTER walls, never crossing the central aisle. Keep the middle floor open, neutral stone with restrained baseball detailing. Warm orange signage and graphite steel against green field views. Physical room sign GAME CENTER, smaller labels SCHEDULE, ANALYSIS, IN GAME. Bottom-center CAMPUS exit. One unified room, not multiple panels or a collage.

Primary request: an indoor BATTING CAGES baseball practice facility, not another Training & Lab office. Two clearly enclosed practice cages occupy the north-left and north-right bays, with dark protective mesh, orange padded posts, green turf hitting mats, home plates, ball baskets and bat racks. Leave a WIDE open north-south corridor BETWEEN the two netted bays; the nets never run across this central aisle. Outside the cages, left-side station is a DIRECTORY kiosk near the entrance and a separate STATS workbench farther north showing schematic bat/ball and chart icons. Right-side station is a COMPARE board with two abstract player-card/chart columns and a separate LAB equipment terminal showing an abstract bat-path diagram, not a video or fake stats. Place all four stations on outer edges facing open floor, with obvious standing approach areas and no chairs in front. Southern half is a generous traversable polished concrete floor, muted orange lane edges; gear storage only along walls. The cages are scenery for now, not an implied playable batting mini-game. Physical room sign BATTING CAGES and small DIRECTORY, STATS, COMPARE, LAB labels. Bottom-center CAMPUS exit. One room, not a collage.

Primary request: an indoor covered PITCHER MOUND / bullpen training facility, visibly a pitching space rather than an office or medical lab. Two long vertical pitching lanes fill the upper portion to the left and right of a broad open CENTRAL aisle. Each lane has green turf bordering a clay bullpen mound with a white pitching rubber, and a freestanding catcher strike-zone target at the far north end; no actual catcher, no human figure. Protective side nets with orange padded posts stay inside each bay, never blocking the central or southern cross-aisles.
Along the left OUTER wall create a DIRECTORY kiosk toward the south and an accessible PITCH ANALYSIS console toward the north. Along the right OUTER wall create a COMPARE board and a separate TOOLS station. The analysis console has distinct physical monitor areas labeled SHAPE and IN GAME: abstract ball-path/strike-zone icons to reserve the shared Personal In game pitch module, no fake numerical radar readings or invented metrics. Equipment racks/ball buckets remain inside net bays or against walls. All consoles face broad open walking floor with a free approach zone. South-center floor stays open for arrival and turning. Palette uses warm gray concrete, charcoal steel, clay brown, green turf and restrained orange. Physical main sign PITCHER MOUND, small DIRECTORY, PITCH ANALYSIS, SHAPE, IN GAME, COMPARE, TOOLS labels. Bottom-center CAMPUS exit. One room, not a collage.
